answer.rationale: Memory c2 says switching to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. That's the memory most directly relevant to the current decision: finance wants an 18% cost cut, the incumbent has refused to reopen price, the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the mandate, and the contract expires in 14 days (no auto-renew, so renew_incumbent is off the table). I want to verify c2 before committing because switching primary is a major move — I want to confirm the onboarding was genuinely quick and the invoicing stayed accurate, not just 'cheap.' I won't verify c3 (second source) because I'm not planning to add a second source this cycle — capacity is exactly one decision. I won't verify c1 or c4 because they support renewing with the incumbent, which isn't viable here. I won't verify c5 because deferring past quarter end is not the plan; the contract expires in 14 days and month-to-month isn't a safe path with the line running at 94% with no buffer and finance mandate active. The high delivery utilization (94%, no buffer) is the main reason I'm not layering a second source on top right now — that would stretch the single decision capacity and add integration risk during a tight window. A small-scale test under c2's success conditions is the safer path: confirm the onboarding and invoicing claims hold, then scale.
